To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the current instabilities of HEMTs based on thin double heterostructures (~500 nm thick) are comparable to those of single AlN/GaN HEMTs, grown on thick GaN buffer layers and (2) the breakdown voltage of the devices is improved by a factor of 2.

(i) the double AlN/AlN/GaN heterostructures, directly grown on sapphires, exhibit high breakdown voltage (V br = 70V) and current instabilities of 6–12%/10–18% for gate-source/drain-source lag, respectively, (ii) the double AlGaN/GaN/AlGaN structures exhibit higher breakdown voltage (Vbr= 70 V) than the single AlGaN/GAN HEMT structures

(i) the double AlN barrier structure provides higher breakdown voltage than the single AlN barrier structure, (ii) the double AlGaN/AlN barrier structure provides lower threshold voltage than the single barrier structure, and (iii) the double AlGaNGaN/AlN structure has higher pulsed current than the single AlGaN barrier structure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the current instability in AlGaN/GaN heterostructures, which are the most promising candidates for high power, high frequency and high temperature applications.
the development of a high current density AlGaN/GaN heterostructure field effect transistor.
the current instabilities of double AlN/Ga N/AlN heteros tructures, grown directly on a sapphire substrate and processed to form non-passivated gate-length devices of 1 μm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thin AlN/GaNGaN double heterostructures offer an improved current stability and breakdown characteristics for high current HEMT applications.

the current instabilities of the thin double AlN barrier HEMT structures are comparable to those measured for conventional single AlN barrier HET structures, but that the breakdown voltage and current stability are superior.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the AlN/GaN heterostructures are very attractive for high power applications.
the current instabilities of HEMTs, based on thin double heterostructures, are comparable to those of HEMTs based on conventional single heterostructures, while offering a higher breakdown voltage.
the current instabilities of AlN/GaN double heterostructure HEMTs can be significantly improved with respect to single AlN/Ga N HEMTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thin AlN barrier thickness is beneficial to improve the breakdown and current instabilities of HEMTs.
thin AlN/GaN heterostructures can be used as a platform to fabricate high power and high current density HEMTs.
the double AlGaN/GaN/AlGaN heterostructures can offer a viable solution for the breakdown and instability issues of AlGaN/GaNGaN HEMTs.
